newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan land prices may have stopped falling -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan land prices may have stopped falling -- EPA.

text.p: Land prices in Japan may have stopped falling, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Tuesday.
Aso also told a regular news conference that the bottoming out of land prices in Japan may start to have a positive effect on the economy.
"Residential land prices may have almost hit a bottom, while I have a feeling that commercial land prices have almost stopped falling," Aso said.
Good commercial land is now attracting buying interest while unattractive commercial land is still in the doldrums, he said.
The government announced on Monday that land prices fell in Japan in 1996 for the sixth successive year, with commercial land prices in cities falling by 11.5 percent.

The National Land Agency said, however, that the pace of the land price declines in major metropolitan areas had been gradually slowing since the latter half of last year and that prices for residential areas were flattening out.
